title: Hazel and the Cover
premise: When a woman named Hazel Voss appears at Gideon Iversen's door claiming he once saved her life in a negotiation he has no memory of, she leaves behind a ledger implicating his late mentor in laundering money for a covert tri-government program. Gideon's investigation reveals the 'favor' was manufactured to recruit him, and the ledger is the inheritance of everyone the program destroyed. Pursued by an assassin erasing witnesses, Gideon and Hazel smuggle the truth across three jurisdictions, discovering the final name in the ledger belongs to Hazel herself. In the end, Gideon breaks every rule he ever followed: he trades himself as hostage for the public release of the files, and Hazel walks free carrying the truth out.
about_author: Tamsin Crane is a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing testimony she was never allowed to comment on. She writes thrillers about people who know exactly how the system sounds when it lies.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Gideon Iversen, suspended after a botched negotiation, answers his door to Hazel Voss, who insists he saved her in Rotterdam twenty years ago — an operation that doesn't exist in any file. She leaves him a coded ledger and vanishes. Reading it, Gideon recognizes his dead mentor's handwriting. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obsession; the past he trusted begins rewriting itself.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Eraser
chapters.summary: Gideon traces the ledger to a joint intelligence slush fund and finds its witnesses dying in orderly accidents. The assassin, Callum Reeve, corners Hazel in Lisbon; she escapes with pages torn from the ledger, and Gideon realizes the final entry names her as the fund's true heir. POV: alternating Gideon and Hazel. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve; two strangers becoming co-conspirators.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Hazel confesses she invented the favor to recruit Gideon — his mentor trained her before the program buried him. Together they broker a handoff with a compromised minister, but Reeve intercepts it, and Gideon chooses to surrender the ledger copy to save Hazel, keeping only what matters: proof of the last victim. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: betrayal transformed into loyalty; rules finally breaking under moral weight.

chapters.title: The Cover
chapters.summary: At a summit in Geneva, Gideon takes the negotiating floor one last time — offering himself as hostage until the files go public, using every skill the system taught him against it. Reeve, revealed as another inherited debt, stands down. Hazel releases the ledger worldwide and disappears with the original. POV: Hazel closing frame. Emotional beat: costly justice; freedom purchased with everything else.
